import java.util.*;
public final class SolutionTest{public static void main(String[]z){assert Arrays.equals(Solution.clampWindow(-2,3,10),new int[]{0,3});assert Arrays.equals(Solution.clampWindow(20,2,10),new int[]{10,10});assert Arrays.equals(Solution.clampWindow(Integer.MAX_VALUE-1,10,Integer.MAX_VALUE),new int[]{Integer.MAX_VALUE-1,Integer.MAX_VALUE});assert Solution.clampWindow(0,-1,1)==null;}}

prompt.text:
Repair the buggy source below without changing the required API.

File contract: Return Solution.java containing public final class Solution.
Required API: public static int[] clampWindow(int start, int size, int length); return null on failure
Behavior: Reject negative size or length. Clamp start into the inclusive range from zero to length, then return the half-open window ending at the smaller of start plus size and length, without arithmetic overflow.
Visible example: With start -2, size 3, and length 10, signed APIs return the window [0,3]; with start beyond length, return the empty window at length.

Buggy source to repair:

public final class Solution { public static int[] clampWindow(int s,int n,int len){if(n<0||len<0)return null;return new int[]{s,Math.min(s+n,len)};} }

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.

reference.code: public final class Solution { public static int[] clampWindow(int s,int n,int len){if(n<0||len<0)return null;s=Math.max(0,Math.min(s,len));int end=n<=len-s?s+n:len;return new int[]{s,end};} }
